column1: # Services known to accept a TOTP authenticator app, by registrable domain.
# HAND-CURATED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. SPEC-V1 §7.4 requires a bundled directory
# and requires its licence to permit redistribution before shipping it. The
# well-known public dataset for this (2fa.directory, formerly twofactorauth.org) is
# a community list whose terms are not unambiguously clear for redistribution inside
# a commercial binary, and whose entries carry no per-entry provenance. Rather than
# ship data whose licence we would be guessing at — the exact failure ADD-001 spent
# a whole addendum avoiding for icons — this list was written for this product and
# is owned by it. Nothing here is copied from that dataset.
# WHAT AN ENTRY MEANS: the service accepts a time-based one-time code from a
# standard authenticator app, on a normal consumer or developer account, without a
# WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN: SMS, email codes, push approval, a hardware key, or a
# vendor's own proprietary app. Those are real second factors and several are
# stronger than TOTP — but they are not what Trynta can help with, and "add a
# one-time code in Trynta" is only actionable when a TOTP app is actually accepted.
# This is why Apple, Steam, Netflix and most retail banks are absent: their second
# factor is real and their users cannot put it here.
# WHAT IT IS NOT: complete. It is a floor, not a census. A service missing from this
# file counts as *not capable*, which is the safe direction — the user is never
# nagged to add a code to something that cannot take one, and the health score's 2FA
# term simply covers fewer items. Adding a service is a data change: append the
# domain, keep the file sorted, rebuild.
# Accuracy over reach. An entry that is wrong produces a nag the user can never
# satisfy, so anything doubtful was left out rather than guessed at.
# One registrable domain (eTLD+1) per line, lowercase, sorted.
